$comment: Tier 1 behavior contract. Kotlin (autofill-core) and Python (apps/api) tests both run every case. Add a case BEFORE changing a rule. `expected: null` means Tier 1 must NOT match (the field goes to Tier 2).

cases.label: Email Address*
cases.why: Punctuation stripped; longest contained alias wins over 'email'.

cases.label: E-mail ID
cases.why: Hyphen becomes a space on both label and alias, so they agree.

cases.label: Current CTC (in LPA)
cases.why: Alias appears as a contiguous phrase; label's only qualifier 'current' is in the alias.

cases.label: Expected CTC
cases.why: 'ctc' (current) is also contained but is blocked by qualifier 'expected' and is shorter.

cases.label: Previous CTC
cases.why: Only 'ctc' is contained; label qualifier 'previous' is missing from it, so it is blocked.

cases.label: Salary
cases.why: Whole-phrase rule: no alias is fully contained. 'salary' alone is not a subset match.

cases.label: Mobile No.
cases.why: No fuzzy matching. The fix is a user-added alias 'mobile no', not a smarter matcher.

cases.label: Emergency contact number
cases.why: 'contact number' is contained but blocked by 'emergency'; the longer alias carries the qualifier.

cases.label: Father's Name
cases.why: Possessive removed before punctuation; qualifier 'father' present in the alias.

cases.label: Last Name
cases.why: 'name' is contained but 'last' is a qualifier it lacks. Prevents filling full name into last name.

cases.label: Address
cases.why: 'address' is not lemmatized to 'addres' (ends in 'ss') and no alias is contained in it.
